description: Echo Chamber is a team of passionate innovators participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project, "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map," aims to make exploring Mars easier by mapping its terrain, identifying potential survival locations, and transforming Martian data into useful insights for future explorers. Together, we're mapping the future of life beyond Earth! 🔴🚀
summary: Ares-Pathfinder is an interactive Martian mapping concept designed to help astronauts plan safer Marswalks. It combines terrain, slope, surface roughness, environmental hazards, radiation context and potential water-ice locations into one decision-support map. Using weighted terrain-cost analysis and A* pathfinding, it compares possible routes and highlights their estimated risks, helping crews make safer and more informed exploration decisions.
details:
Ares-Pathfinder: Dynamic Risk & Opportunity Map

The Problem

Exploring Mars on foot will be challenging and potentially dangerous. Astronauts must navigate steep slopes, loose sand, rocky terrain, extreme temperatures, radiation exposure and dust storms while managing limited oxygen, battery power and mission time.

Existing mapping tools provide valuable scientific information, but mission crews may need to interpret several separate datasets to understand the risks of an entire route.

Our Solution

Ares-Pathfinder is a layered Martian mapping and route-planning concept that brings multiple scientific datasets together into one interface.

It helps answer three important questions:

  1. Where can astronauts safely travel?
  2. What environmental and geological hazards could affect their journey?
  3. Which locations may offer valuable scientific discoveries or resources?

How It Works

The system combines terrain, elevation, surface imagery and environmental information to create a weighted traversability cost map.

A* pathfinding is then used to calculate and compare possible routes between a starting point and a destination. Each route can be evaluated according to its estimated terrain cost, distance and associated risks.

The map can display potential hazards and exploration opportunities, allowing astronauts and mission planners to understand the trade-offs between different routes.

Data Sources

The proposed system uses data from several NASA missions and scientific projects:

  • HiRISE imagery for high-resolution Martian surface observations.
  • MOLA elevation data for terrain and slope analysis.
  • AI4Mars for labelled terrain information.
  • Curiosity rover RAD measurements for surface radiation context.
  • Mars Climate Sounder for atmospheric and dust-related context.
  • SHARAD radar observations and SWIM products for subsurface and water-ice information.
  • Historical rover mission records for location-based scientific context.

Innovative Features

Subsurface Sonar: A proposed auditory interface that translates selected SHARAD interpretations into sound cues, helping users understand possible subsurface ice and geological structures.

Cognitive Vitality Index: An experimental landscape-analysis concept that identifies visually and geologically interesting locations using image-derived metrics.

AI Mission Historian: A proposed feature that connects historical rover discoveries and observations to their geographical locations.

Expected Impact

Ares-Pathfinder aims to make Martian exploration safer and more informed by bringing scientific information and route-planning decisions together. It could help astronauts understand terrain challenges, compare alternative routes, identify possible resources and discover scientifically interesting locations.

Future Development

Future improvements include integrating more validated NASA datasets, improving terrain classification, introducing uncertainty-aware risk scoring, testing realistic EVA scenarios and exploring offline operation and suit-compatible displays.

Ares-Pathfinder is a decision-support concept and requires extensive scientific, technical and operational validation before any real mission use.
